question: Does preserving only a winning label, using an arbitrary nonlinear encoding, evade the state requirement imposed by arbitrary individual-cell deletions?
contract: A strictly positive integer association table with at least two rows and two outputs. A query supplies nonnegative rational row weights and any subset of surviving cells. Return only the lowest-index winning output; no scores or tie sets are exposed. A deletion means zeroing an individual aggregate cell, not subtracting an externally supplied episode contribution.
candidateArgument: Surviving cells in different rows and outputs expose their ratio through weighted comparisons. The resulting comparison graph is connected except at 2x2. Three-cell comparisons bridge that exceptional case. Thus the entire positive table is identifiable up to one global positive scale, independently of how an internal representation is encoded.
experiment: Reconstruct normalized tables from a winner-only callable using exact rational queries. The reconstructor receives dimensions and the integer bound, never the table or its scores. Binary-search a finite rational candidate grid at midpoints, so comparison queries never rely on a tie answer.
acceptance: Every reconstructed rational coordinate equals the original coordinate divided by cell (0,0). Retain every winner query and reconstructed case. Any mismatch rejects the constructive argument.
controls: Check global-scale equivalence, the disconnected 2x2 comparison graph and its three-cell bridge, maxWeight=1, and a one-row non-identifiability example. Reject zero, negative and out-of-bound weights in this strictly positive experiment.
interpretation: An exact representation supporting every declared deletion and cue must distinguish projective classes of tables. This does not forbid compression of structure, approximation, restricted cues, bounded deletions, whole-row mutations, or caller-supplied additive removal. It does not establish a lower bound for arbitrary natural-language memories or shipping vector search.
priorArtBoundary: Utility elicitation and uniqueness of linear utilities are established decision theory. This is a memory-contract derivation and falsifiable extension of the earlier linear screen; no claim of a new general theorem or an invention. No speed, byte-saving, real-memory-utility or competitive claim follows from this experiment.
resources: Standard-library exact arithmetic, one local process, no models or paid services. Calibration and the frozen remote soak remain unchanged.
